A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Achieving Approximate Symmetry Is Exponentially Easier than Exact Symmetry. Their main text, equations, figures, references, and Appendices A–G are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Appendix G and Figure 2 report original synthetic regression experiments, including test loss versus averaging-subset size and training epoch.

after.justification: Appendix G and Figure 2 retain the original synthetic regression experiments and their measured test-loss results.

M1.justification: The action-query framework, linear averaging operator, and random group-sampling construction remain unchanged. Appendix G uses the same neural network and test-time averaging procedure. The new complex-valued remarks concern theoretical scope.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the 100-element rotation-group illustration and the 20-dimensional Gaussian regression task with coordinate-wise sign-flip symmetry. No evaluated datasets, domains, or task scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Figure 2 retains the same unaveraged baseline and averaging comparisons. Figure 1 retains the original function and averages over 5 and 100 rotations. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Appendix G retains 50,000 training and 50,000 test samples, hidden widths 128 and 64, SGD with learning rate 0.001, batch size 256, and 500 epochs. Squared-loss evaluation and subset sizes 2^k for k=0,...,10 are unchanged.

E4.justification: The subset-size sensitivity analysis and comparison across training epochs in Figure 2 are unchanged. No new empirical ablation, robustness test, error analysis, or case study appears.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies experimental repeat counts or seeds or reports error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The revised high-probability statements in Appendix A.8 concern theoretical guarantees.

E6.justification: The empirical appendix, plotted results, and figure captions are unchanged. Both versions report most averaging benefits by subset size 32, marginal gains thereafter, and improved test loss throughout training relative to the unaveraged baseline.

T1.justification: Appendix C.1 adds a Molien-formula proof for Claim 24, corresponding to v1's cited but unproved Claim 22. Appendix A.8 redefines risk as expectation over label noise and replaces expected inverse-Gram bounds with high-probability bounds over inputs, changing the sample requirement from n≥c3m to n≥c0c1 log(m/δ). Appendix F adds a 1-Lipschitz assumption and replaces the size(ω)^(-1/d) Wasserstein rate with sqrt(|G|/size(ω)). Section 3 revises function-space assumptions and states complex-valued extensions; Equation (4.2) explicitly becomes an upper bound on K. These substantially revise the theoretical support and qualifications.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the averaging-complexity framework, the claimed first theoretical separation, and the central linear-versus-logarithmic dependence on group size. The added proofs support these existing contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix A.8 now qualifies its generalization conclusions as high-probability guarantees over sampled inputs. Appendix F adds regularity qualifications and revises its limitation discussion to require Θ(|G|) averaging in the general Lipschitz setting, describing exponential dependence on dimension as occurring often rather than universally.

D1.justification: Appendix G retains the same data-generation instructions, target function, network architecture, optimizer settings, and fixed-subset evaluation procedure. No implementation, hardware, runtime, or code/data-access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 1 adds citations to Dao et al. (2019), Chen et al. (2020), and Patil and Du (2023). Appendix F adds Han et al. (2015) to support its revised minimax discussion. The broader positioning and novelty claim remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose and notation edits, adds two explanatory remarks and acknowledgments, and changes the header to the ICLR 2026 publication designation. The overall narrative and section ordering remain stable; the new proof creates an additional subsection in Appendix C.

P2.justification: Existing material is reflowed, some mathematical displays are expanded, and Figure 2 changes position on the final page. Figures 1 and 2 retain the same panels, axes, legends, and captions. No figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: v2 improves theoretical checkability by supplying an explicit proof for the previously cited claim in Appendix C.1 and clarifying the randomness and sample-size conditions behind Appendix A.8's generalization guarantees. Appendix F also adds regularity qualifications. These are focused improvements to the existing theoretical case. The unexplained extra c introduced in Equation (A.53) is a small regression, but does not outweigh those gains.
